generated.title: Why Does the Earth Shake? (Improved Version) | Earthquake Science for Kids
generated.description:
Why does the Earth shake? Earth's outer shell is cracked into huge pieces called tectonic plates. They move super slowly, and sometimes their edges get stuck. Stress builds up, then the rocks suddenly slip and let out a burst of energy that travels outward as seismic waves. That's what makes the ground shake!

Scientists study seismic waves to learn about our planet. What will you discover?

This is the improved version: the seismic waves now start from an underground source, shown in a ground cross-section.

Part of the Earthquake Science for Kids series from Next Huge Quake.
